name: Chip supply
summary: Helium shortage and the 10 Nov rare-earth deadline weigh on chip supply
state: Qatar supplies about a third of the world's helium, which chip fabs need, and Hormuz disruption has tightened supply. China's rare-earth export-control pause expires on 10 Nov. Chip shares fell sharply on 2 Nov on doubts about AI spending (Saxo), but no major TSMC or Samsung output stoppage had been reported as of 3 Nov.
for_you: Possible delays or higher prices for electronics; no shortage in shops yet.
rubric_hit: Shortages in key inputs; no fab outage = Watch

sources.title: MarketScreener — Helium shortage threatens semiconductor industry

why: Advanced chips underpin everything from phones to AI to weapons; supply is concentrated in Taiwan and Korea.
drivers: Export controls, Taiwan risk, fab outages, AI demand, materials.

rubric.alert: Major disruption to TSMC/Samsung output, or controls halting a major supply chain.
rubric.watch: New export controls, shortages reported in key segments, or a fab outage.
rubric.normal: Supply normal; no new major controls.
